shortDescription: NAS Server operations for PowerStore Storage system

options.name: array_ip
options.description: IP or FQDN of the PowerStore management system.

options.name: current_node
options.description: Unique identifier or name of the node on which the NAS server is running.

options.name: current_unix_directory_service
options.description: Define the Unix directory service used for looking up identity information for Unix such as UIDs, GIDs, net groups, and so on.

options.name: default_unix_user
options.description: Default Unix user name used for granting access in case of Windows to Unix user mapping failure. When empty, access in such case is denied.

options.name: default_windows_user
options.description: Default Windows user name used for granting access in case of Unix to Windows user mapping failure. When empty, access in such case is denied.

options.name: description
options.description: Description of the NAS server.

options.name: is_auto_user_mapping_enabled
options.description: To automatically generate the unix user (uid), if the windows user does not have any in the configured Unix Directory Service (UDS). In a pure SMB or non multi-protocol environment, this should be set to true.

options.name: is_username_translation_enabled
options.description: Enable the possibility to match a Windows account with an Unix account with different names.

options.name: nas_server_id
options.description: Unique id of the NAS server. Mutually exclusive with I(nas_server_name).

options.name: nas_server_name
options.description: Name of the NAS server. Mutually exclusive with I(nas_server_id).

options.name: nas_server_new_name
options.description: New name of the NAS server for a rename operation.

options.name: password
options.description: The password of the PowerStore host.

options.name: performance_policy
options.description: The File Performance policy name or ID for the NAS server. Associates a file IO limit rule policy with the NAS server for bandwidth control. Requires PowerStoreOS 4.1 or later. To represent policy, both name or ID can be used interchangeably. The module will detect both. A NAS server can be assigned a performance policy at the time of creation or later. The policy can also be changed for a given NAS server by simply passing the new value. To remove the performance policy from a NAS server, pass

options.name: port
options.description: Port number for the PowerStore array. If not passed, it will take 443 as default.

options.name: preferred_node
options.description: Unique identifier or name of the preferred node for the NAS server. The initial value (on NAS server create) is taken from the current node.

options.name: protection_policy
options.description: Name/ID of the protection policy applied to the nas server. Policy can be removed by passing an empty string in the I(protection_policy) parameter.

options.name: state
options.description: Define whether the nas server should exist or not.

options.name: timeout
options.description: Time after which the connection will get terminated. It is to be mentioned in seconds.

options.name: user
options.description: The username of the PowerStore host.

options.name: validate_certs
options.description: Boolean variable to specify whether to validate SSL certificate or not. C(true) - indicates that the SSL certificate should be verified. Set the environment variable REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE to the path of the SSL certificate. C(false) - indicates that the SSL certificate should not be verified.
